representations?"}],"feedback_interpretation":"Recent outcomes strengthen the decision to measure local response curves. The m125 1/1, 100-uL, 500-uL point measured 13.44/38.40 mL and the pure-EA counterpart measured 8.69/22.11 mL, confirming that the loading-solvent-volume association is composition-dependent rather than a universal shift. The m207 5/1 results now span 50, 100, and 150 uL with materially different endpoints, supporting loading-conditioned curves. The m120 5/1, 50-uL point was extremely late while the 100-uL point was much earlier, so the next labels target loading-matched composition bridges rather than linear interpolation. The m92 PE/EA pair at 1/1 and 50 uL showed a real loading-solvent-identity contrast, while its 20/1 result was close to the revised prediction; this argues for selective condition-response testing rather than a broad solvent-identity correction. Recent m178 and m159 labels confirmed severe historical underprediction in weak-eluent tails, whereas m91 remained comparatively early and m177 showed a strong loading-dependent V2 effect. I therefore use matched curves around m78, m177, m178, and m207, while adding chemically distinct sulfur, heteroaromatic, alcohol, nitrile, and ester neighborhoods to test transfer. Historical errors are treated as acquisition-time evidence; current candidate predictions are used to locate discriminating conditions, not reported as measured errors.","batch_rationale":"The batch repairs several known failure regions while preserving scientifically meaningful local experiments. Four m78, three m177, and three m178 conditions form fixed-loading composition curves around observed threshold or endpoint anomalies. Three m207 conditions and three m92 conditions probe composition at loadings where recent measurements showed non-interpolation behavior. The m125 and m120 choices extend loading-solvent and sample-volume interactions, including conditions that can distinguish composition effects from loading effects. m199, m117, m159, m95, m128, m91, m67, m90, m141, m146, and m129 add distinct structural neighborhoods with measured late tails, early exceptions, or positional-transfer failures. This combination should improve generalization by teaching both local response geometry and scaffold-conditioned transfer across the Row-distribution. The choices are condition-novel and frozen as one batch; no prediction interval is treated as uncertainty, and no endpoint magnitude is an acquisition objective."}
